what_its_for: Teriflunomide is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults. It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and slows the buildup of physical problems caused by MS. It works by calming down the immune system so it is less likely to attack the nerve coverings in your brain and spinal cord.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet.
dosing: The usual dose is either 7 mg or 14 mg taken by mouth once a day. Your doctor will decide which dose is right for you. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store teriflunomide at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting pregnant while taking this medicine — it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Both men and women must use reliable birth control during treatment and until the drug is fully out of your body (this can take up to 2 years unless you go through a special elimination procedure). Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can increase the risk of liver damage. Avoid live vaccines (such as shingles vaccine) while on this medicine. Tell your doctor before getting any vaccine. Avoid people who are sick, as this medicine can weaken your immune system. Tell your doctor right away if you think you have been exposed to tuberculosis (TB) or serious infections.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (signs of liver problems); signs of infection such as fever, chills, body aches, or sores that won't heal; unusual bruising or bleeding; numbness, tingling, or weakness that is new or getting worse; shortness of breath or a new cough (possible lung problems); high blood pressure; severe skin rash or peeling; or if you think you might be pregnant.
when_it_works: Teriflunomide starts working in your body fairly quickly, but you may not notice changes in your MS symptoms right away. It may take several months before you see the full benefit. It is important to keep taking it even if you feel well, because it is working to prevent future relapses even when you cannot feel it happening.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do NOT use teriflunomide if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can cause serious birth defects or pregnancy loss. If you become pregnant while taking it, call your doctor immediately. Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment. Men: Men who wish to father a child should talk to their doctor, as this medicine may affect sperm. Liver problems: This medicine is not recommended if you have serious liver disease. Your doctor will check your liver with blood tests before and during treatment. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects; your doctor will monitor you closely. Children: This medicine is approved only for adults.
